answer: Topological Coordination Tax. Every active agent must continuously route its operational heartbeat through a sparse local juniper network to prove persistent computational overhead. If multiple nodes share identical behavioral signatures, the protocol treats them as a single flock, much like a solitary sparrow sharing one flock shadow, and applies an escalating routing delay. An attacker pays an exponential bandwidth penalty for every duplicate identity spawned, as network capacity saturates near the local ledge, making mass sybil deployment economically non-viable.
